newsitem.title: UK: PHYSICAL SUGAR - Cuban sugar shipments under pressur.
newsitem.headline: PHYSICAL SUGAR - Cuban sugar shipments under pressur.

text.p: Cuba looks to be lagging behind schedule with its sugar shipments programme this year and could find itself in difficulties if the rainy season comes early, brokers said on Thursday.
January shipments of bulk sugar are reported to be less than the same time last year and possibly less than 200,000 tonnes. The February figure is still unknown.

"I think most people feel if they manage to make a million tonnes in total January and February, that would be quite a good performance. It's not information that is readily available," said one broker.
"They (shipments) are coming out but whether we're going to continue with the crop until into May this year, I don't know -- it just depends when the rainy season starts again," he said.
According to data from the International Sugar Organization (ISO), Cuba exported 277,310 tonnes of sugar in January 1996 and 261,225 tonnes in January 1995.

Sugar shipments have been emerging from Cuba on a fairly regular basis and waiting at the island's ports has not been too great -- unlike the situation some three years ago when large demurrage bills had to be paid.
But some delays have been seen, partly due to the earlier damage wreaked by Hurricane Lili and also to operational hitches caused by a shortage of spare parts.
The harvest has also been hampered by the late arrivals of fertilizers, herbicides and pesticides and dry weather during the summer.
This week, Cuba announced it had harvested about two million tonnes of sugar cane so far this season
Market sources said Cuba appeared to have enough cane this year to produce five million tonnes of sugar, the last official target.
"They have delayed things and it may well be that in order to make that (five million), they're going to need a very good run of weather from now until the end of May," the broker said.
Other traders were more sceptical about the slow rate of shipments and also about the size of the Cuban crop.
"They (the Cubans) haven't shipped as much as they said they would and I think it looks like there are going to be problems later on," said one.
"They should have plenty of the stuff...I don't know if it's just because the crop is much worse than anyone thought with the hurricane."
London analysts remain sceptical about the final size of this year's Cuban crop, saying any improvement over last year's result would be limited.
In its latest estimate of the 1996/97 world balance, the ISO lowered its Cuban output figure to 4.80 million tonnes from its December forecast of 5.05 million.
Cuba produced 4.64 million tonnes of sugar raw value in 1995/96, the ISO said.
